messages:
alice: Heads-up — canary p99 spiked from 190ms -> 420ms at ~15:03 UTC after last rollout. Dashboard: https://redwood-infra.prod/d/latency/canary?from=now-1h :eyes:

bob: I saw that alert. GPU timeline shows an extra memcpy and a heavy kernel that wasn't hot before — looks like a different MatMul kernel selected mid-sequence.

carla: Can we get an `nsys`/perfetto trace for one of the affected requests? Need to see kernel timeline + nvtx ranges.

alice: Thinking low-impact approach first: sample 0.5% of live requests for 5m with userland trace id pins, and independently run an nsys capture on a synthetic repro to get full kernel timings. Estimate: sampling adds ~0.07% latency at p50 for sampled reqs, overall traffic overhead <0.001.

daniel: For the synthetic run use:
```
nsys profile -o repro_207123 -t nvtx,cuda,osrt --sample=cpu --cpuctxsw=false --capture-range=nvtx --force-overwrite --trace-fork=false ./repro_load --concurrency 8 --requests 500
```
Add `--sample=clock` if you want lower overhead but coarser GPU timing.

evan: FYI perfetto/full GPU traces add non-trivial overhead if you attach to all processes — on small sequences we've seen 6-12% extra tail latency. That's why I prefer targeted `nsys` on a repro instance and tiny eBPF counters in-prod.

carla: Also check KV cache hit/miss delta around the spike. If cache miss rate increased, that could trigger a different batching path which picks the generic kernel. Add a metric: `runtime.kv_cache.hit_rate` with trace_id label for correlation.

alice: profiler-bot started an async low-impact sample run: config -> rate=0.5%, window=300s, attach=trace-id header. Bot says file will be uploaded to s3 when complete.

profiler-bot: nsys run queued on repro host i-0abcde, expected runtime ~120s. Upload target: s3://redwood-traces/2071234567/repro_207123.nsys

bob: Quick local nvprof snippet from the repro showed this pattern: heavier `matmul_generic` kernel + a 2.1ms memcpy right before kernel launch. Could be a kernel-selection regression in the dispatcher heuristics.

carla: Proposed guardrails for safe-prod profiling:
- max_sample_rate: "1%"
- sample_window_secs: "30"
- max_concurrent_samples_per_host: "2"
- fallback: "cpu-only" if GPU utilization > 85%
- disable_during_bursty_load: "true"
- attach_trace_id_header: "true"

daniel: Agreed. Also, ensure sampled requests set `X-Trace-Mode: minimal` header so downstream services don't cascade traces. Add a toggle to exclude KV-heavy endpoints.

evan: For overhead estimates I ran a microbench:
```
# baseline (no sampler)
p50: 22ms p99: 187ms
# sample 1% (eBPF hit counter + header tagging)
p50: 22.1ms p99: 191ms (0.02% p50 delta, +2% p99 on sampled requests only)
# full nsys capture on repro (not in-prod)
p50: 23ms p99: 210ms (full-trace overhead ~6% measured on repro)
```
Numbers show sampling is low impact if we keep rate <=1% and bounded windows.

alice: Action items:
1) evan -> run 3 low-impact samples across different AZs (0.5% x 5m) and upload traces (due EOD).
2) daniel -> nsys capture on repro host and attach nvtx markers around dispatcher (PR for nvtx markers if missing).
3) carla -> instrument KV cache hit/miss counters + expose `trace_id` label in metrics (PR #789).
4) bob -> investigate kernel-selector change in last deploy, look for diff in kernel priority table / heuristic fallback.
5) alice -> prepare rollback play if p99 stays >350ms for 10m.

bob: I'll also run a quick A/B with older kernel table pinned to confirm. If p99 drops, we have a strong signal.

carla: +1. Also add a runtime guard: if sample_count_today > 10k then autoscale sample_rate down to keep overhead budget.

alice: Perfect. Please log progress in this thread and attach trace IDs. :thumbsup:
